- effect_estimate: In Prince Albert, the "leiwater" irrigation-furrow water allocation is legally restricted to residents holding allocation rights recorded in historical (Apartheid-era) title deeds, structurally excluding North-End (predominantly Colored) residents from that supply while South-End (historically white-favored) residents retain access; municipal-reported access is 97.7% with 70% having piped water inside dwellings, but access and reliability differ sharply by area. In HaSinari, the municipal water department has failed entirely: residents wait an average of two weeks for taps to run (2-3 hours/day when running), and Water Committees -- elected, fee-funded community bodies -- have taken over de facto water governance, collecting monthly household contributions to fund diesel for borehole pumps in place of the state.
